summary: Interrogated the PH-1 plan against the code it changes and the suite that exercises it. Two answers were missing and one risk was materially understated; all three were fixed in the plan before this grill was recorded. The scope boundary against PH-2, PH-3 and PH-4 held under pressure.
gaps: The plan said the shared parser goes 'beside the existing frontmatter parsers', but there are three of those — in plans.py, specs.py and record_signoff.py — and the story's whole point is that ONE function serves both the gate and, later, the board. An unnamed home is how two copies appear.

The plan's ordering risk was stated as 'a repo scaffolded between the two commits would fail sign-off'. Verification against the suite shows it is far larger: the repo fixture builds every test repo with forge.py init, which copies BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md into docs/product/BRIEF.md, and the shared sign_off() helper asserts record_signoff.py exits 0. Dozens of tests call sign_off, so an unrealigned template fails most of the suite, not one scaffold.
The plan did not say what 'an empty heading body' means. A word-count or length threshold would refuse a legitimately terse constraints list.
The plan claimed the board would call the same parser, but PH-4 is a different story in a different worktree and nothing in PH-1 can enforce that.
resolutions: The parser is named to factory_lib.py, with the reason: record_signoff.py is a top-level script importing from factory_lib, PH-4's board code imports from forge_cli, and factory_lib is the only module both already depend on.

The risk section now states the suite-wide coupling and turns it into the argument for the task order — the suite is itself the regression test for template drift, going red across the board rather than letting a client discover it at their own sign-off.
The risk section fixes the semantics: empty means no non-whitespace content, never a length threshold.
The acceptance criterion is scoped to what PH-1 can prove — one parser exists and the gate calls it. Whether PH-4 reuses it is PH-4's acceptance criterion, and the spec states it for that story.
open_items: non-blocking: sign-off is a one-time gate, so a brief that degrades after sign-off is never re-checked. forge doctor reports it, which is the level of enforcement a one-time gate can honestly carry.

non-blocking: doctor mixes machine checks with project-artifact checks. Precedent already exists there (prose_verify_commands, legacy_required_tests), so this story follows it rather than opening a separate reporting surface.
